title: Haptic resize rails and contextual density controls for virtual grid
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Our virtualized data grid currently offers column resizing and density modes, but users report poor discoverability for density presets, janky resizing at high row counts, and difficulty making fine-grained width adjustments when using touch/trackpad. Goals: 1) Introduce a rail-based resize affordance that provides tactile (visual) feedback and snaplines for common column widths; 2) Surface contextual density controls (Quick presets + per-table custom preference) that persist across sessions; 3) Improve resize performance under virtualization (reduce reflow / measurement thrash) and provide a live preview mode that doesn't re-render entire row set; 4) Ensure keyboard and assistive tech parity for all controls.
acceptance_criteria: Add a slim resize rail (8px hit area) that appears on column hover and remains visible when resizing; rails should show faint snaplines at 25%, 50%, 75% of typical column widths.
Introduce three default density presets: Flow (default), Cozy, Compact — accessible from header kebab and persisted via user preference storage.

Live-resize preview must use placeholder overlay + off-main-thread measurement to avoid full row reflow; resizing a column on a 100k-row virtualized table should not exceed 30ms frame jank budget for the initial drag response.
Provide an opt-in haptic affordance in the prototype (vibration API on supported devices) and clear fallback visuals when vibration is unavailable.
All interactions must be reachable by keyboard (tab to header, arrow keys to adjust width with shift modifier for 10px jumps) and announce width changes to screen readers.

Design tokens used for rails, snaplines, and density spacing must map to token names in the design system (spacing.grid-x, token.surface-rail, token.snapline-emphasis) so engineering can implement without token mapping work.
Deliver Figma spec with states (hover, active, snapping, keyboard adjustments) and a short motion spec for the rail reveal/-hide transition.
Include at least two user-testing snippets from internal PM/SE interviews showing improved discoverability for density presets.
Update Console docs and change log explaining density defaults, how to set per-table preferences, and migration notes for existing users.
Design sign-off from PM and accessibility review completed (a11y checklist ticked).
design_notes: Prefer subtle visual affordances over persistent heavy UI — rails should not increase perceived column gutter unless being interacted with.
Snaplines derived from heuristic: common content breakpoints (timestamp column, short label, long text) — team will run telemetry survey (ENG-8812) to validate top three snap widths per column type.
Density presets intentionally named to avoid user confusion with 'compact' being the smallest; 'Flow' emphasizes comfortable reading with variable row-height rhythm.
Prototype uses CSS containment and will try to leverage virtual DOM diffing hints to avoid re-rendering unchanged cells; ENG will provide guidance for mutation strategy.
Haptic/vibration is optional and gated behind navigator.vibrate availability; include a feature flag for internal testing.
Provide microcopy for persistence control: 'Remember density for this table' with clear opt-out in table settings.
Edge case: column groups and frozen columns should expose rail only for resizable columns; frozen column resizes must reflect in adjacent non-frozen area with smooth handoff.
Performance goal: avoid layout thrash by reading layout values once on drag start and writing CSS transforms rather than adjusting width on every pointermove when possible.
